# Human preference reward model v18: frozen study

**Status:** protocol frozen before reading any held-out test rows. The test Arrow cache was generated by the dataset loader during train-only preparation; its records have not been inspected or used for selection.

## Question

Can a small reward head trained on human helpfulness comparisons rank a held-out preferred response above its paired alternative, and does it outperform a response-length baseline?

The study uses only the `helpful-base` portion of Anthropic HH-RLHF at revision `09be8c5bbc57cb3887f3a9732ad6aa7ec602a1fa`. The dataset card describes this data as preference comparisons suitable for preference/reward modeling and states the MIT license. The study trains no dialogue policy and makes no claims about assistant quality, safety, or capability. See the [dataset card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anthropic/hh-rlhf) and [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.05862).

## Frozen design

The machine-readable protocol is [`protocols/cpu_lm_hh_reward_v18.json`](../protocols/cpu_lm_hh_reward_v18.json); its adjacent lock file stores the canonical SHA256 digest. It fixes the dataset/model revisions, CPU-only resource limits, source split row pools, deterministic hash-ranked selection, exclusions for pilot contexts, feature definition, optimizer, baselines, metrics, and pass rules.

Three disjoint cohorts of 128 human preference pairs train three linear scalar reward heads. The language model is frozen and used only to compute mean final-layer hidden features for each response. The learned head optimizes pairwise logistic loss. A separate set of 256 test-split pairs is used only for development selection. If and only if every development gate passes, a separate 256-pair pool may be opened for confirmation. Context hashes may not cross cohorts. Invalid or duplicate contexts are skipped in the frozen candidate order; a shortfall is reported without widening the pool.

Each arm is compared with chance and a longer-response baseline. The gates require mean preference accuracy of at least 0.55, NLL below 0.68, at least a 0.03 accuracy gain over the length baseline, and a positive lower endpoint for a paired per-example bootstrap interval. The confirmation gate is identical. Metrics include Brier score and 10-bin equal-width expected calibration error. Runtime, memory, pinned input/model hashes, exclusions, and auditor outputs will be recorded.

## Interpretation limits

A pass would support only the narrow claim that this frozen reward head predicts the dataset's human pairwise preference labels on the declared held-out subset. It would not show that users prefer a resulting assistant, that model behavior is safer, or that language-model capability improved. The source contains sensitive and sometimes upsetting content; public artifacts will contain hashes and aggregate results, not raw dialogue text.

## Access and artifacts

The source dataset cache was produced during train-only feasibility preparation. The official test Arrow file was generated automatically, but no held-out row contents were read. The index partition and deterministic selection method are fixed here; development rows may be decoded only after this protocol and runner/auditor are committed. Confirmation indices 512–1023 remain reserved unless the development gate passes. Only local CPU and cached model/data are used; no paid compute or GPU is required.
